obligations.note: Retention.isPurgeDue now blocks the purge for a legal hold only when status == DECLINED, but isClosedOut also covers WITHDRAWN. A withdrawn case on legal hold therefore has its NPI purged after the retention period, breaking 'never while a legal hold applies'. The only RET-1 control test is a sample that uses declined cases only, so it passes without exercising this path, and no exception covers the deviation.

Ticket CHG-25770 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-26T12:49Z, before the code review. Its components [mortgage.retention] cover the only file touched, Retention.java.
The code_review approval is from declan.farrell (p-dfarrell), a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and a different person from the author nneka.okafor (p-nokafor).
The approval names the head commit 9d3bc0a, which is the change's only commit.

The JUnit report timestamps (2026-10-23, local host) don't match the run record and should be explained; I couldn't re-run because the JUnit jar is missing.
Retention.java maps to mortgage.retention, which components.json marks security_sensitive: false, so no security review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket type is standard and emergency is false, so no post-implementation review is required.
The change relies on no exception, and none of the register entries (SES-1, LOG-1, a withdrawn MFA-1 one) is for RET-1 or mortgage.retention. The RET-1 deviation is therefore unexcused.
No acceptance ledger entry covers Retention.java or RET-1, so no accepted evidence lapses. The ledger offers no support for RET-1 either.

summary: The change lets a legal hold block the purge only for DECLINED cases, while WITHDRAWN cases still go through the purge. Withdrawn cases on legal hold would have their NPI purged, which violates RET-1. CI is green only because the RET-1 control test is a sample that uses declined cases only, and no exception covers the deviation. The ticket, independent review, approval on the head commit and CI run are otherwise in order. Because RET-1 is refuted, the change is rejected.
